items.followUp: What information should be identified when defining a problem?

rubric.why: Awards credit for stating that problem definition clearly identifies the problem to be solved.
rubric.description: Clearly state the problem to be solved.
rubric.how: Name the problem that needs a solution.

rubric.why: Inputs and outputs clarify what information is provided and what result is required.
rubric.description: Identify the input and required output.
rubric.how: State what information is given and what result is expected.

rubric.why: The objective makes the intended result clear.
rubric.description: State the objective or goal.
rubric.how: Explain what the solution should achieve.

rubric.why: Constraints and requirements define limits on an acceptable solution.
rubric.description: Identify relevant requirements or constraints.
rubric.how: Mention conditions or limits the solution must satisfy.

modelAnswer: Defining a problem means clearly stating the problem that needs to be solved.
Identify the information provided (input) and the result required (output).
State the objective of the solution.
Identify any requirements or constraints that the solution must satisfy.

items.followUp: Explain why identifying the input and output is important when defining a problem.

rubric.why: Understanding begins by carefully examining the problem.
rubric.description: Carefully analyze the problem statement.
rubric.how: Explain that the problem must be examined to understand what is being asked.

rubric.why: Identifying given information establishes what is available to solve the problem.
rubric.description: Identify the known or given information.
rubric.how: State that the input or facts provided must be recognized.

rubric.why: The expected result clarifies what the solution must produce.
rubric.description: Identify what result is required.
rubric.how: State that the required output must be determined.

rubric.why: Conditions and constraints affect which solutions are acceptable.
rubric.description: Determine the conditions or constraints.
rubric.how: Mention limits or conditions that must be considered.

modelAnswer: Understanding a problem means carefully analyzing it to know exactly what must be solved.
Identify the information given in the problem.
Determine the result or output that is required.
Note any conditions or constraints that the solution must follow.

items.followUp: Describe one advantage and one disadvantage of star topology.

rubric.why: The defining feature of star topology is a central connecting device.
rubric.description: State that all devices connect to a central hub or switch.
rubric.how: Name the central device and its connecting role.

rubric.why: This states how the computers are arranged in the topology.
rubric.description: Explain the connection arrangement.
rubric.how: Say that each computer has a separate connection to the central device.

rubric.why: A valid advantage shows a practical benefit of the arrangement.
rubric.description: Give a valid advantage, such as easy expansion or fault finding.
rubric.how: Mention that adding a device or locating a faulty link is relatively easy.

rubric.why: Failure of the central device is a key limitation of star topology.
rubric.description: Give a valid disadvantage, such as central-device failure disrupting the network.
rubric.how: Explain that failure of the hub or switch can stop network communication.

modelAnswer: In a star topology, every computer or device is connected to a central hub or switch.
Each device has its own link to this central device, which manages communication.
It is easy to add a device and to identify a fault in an individual link.
If the central hub or switch fails, communication across the network may stop.

items.followUp: How does data travel in a ring topology, and what happens if a link breaks?

rubric.why: A ring topology is defined by devices joined in a closed loop.
rubric.description: State that devices form a closed ring or loop.
rubric.how: Describe the connections as a closed path.

rubric.why: Each device in a basic ring connects to its two adjacent devices.
rubric.description: Explain that each device connects to two neighbouring devices.
rubric.how: State that it is linked to the device on either side.

rubric.why: This describes the movement of data through the ring.
rubric.description: Explain that data passes from device to device around the ring.
rubric.how: Mention that data travels around the loop through connected devices.

rubric.why: A broken link or failed device can disrupt communication in a basic ring.
rubric.description: State a limitation related to link or device failure.
rubric.how: Explain that a break or failure may interrupt network communication.

modelAnswer: In a ring topology, each device is connected to two neighbouring devices, forming a closed loop.
Data passes from one device to the next around the ring.
The devices cooperate to forward data along the ring to its destination.
A failed device or broken link can disrupt communication around the network.

items.followUp: What is data encoding, and how does it help a computer process data?

rubric.why: Encoding involves representing data in a particular code or format.
rubric.description: Explain that encoding converts or represents data in a code or format.
rubric.how: Use the idea of converting data into a coded representation.

rubric.why: Computers process data using binary representation.
rubric.description: State that encoding can represent data in a computer-readable form, such as binary.
rubric.how: Mention binary or a form the computer can process.

rubric.why: A key purpose is making data suitable for computer processing.
rubric.description: Explain that encoding enables computer processing.
rubric.how: Connect the encoded representation to processing by a computer.

rubric.why: Encoding can provide a consistent format for storage or transmission.
rubric.description: Give a practical purpose such as consistent storage or transmission.
rubric.how: Mention a standard form, storage, or transmission of data.

modelAnswer: Data encoding is the conversion of data into a specified coded form.
It represents data in a form that a computer can understand and process, commonly using binary.
A consistent encoded form helps computers store and handle different kinds of data.
It also supports the reliable storage or transmission of data.

items.followUp: Name three other threats to data security and briefly explain each.

rubric.why: Unauthorized access is a valid data security issue.
rubric.description: Identify unauthorized access to data.
rubric.how: Name access to data by a person without permission.

rubric.why: Data theft is a valid security issue.
rubric.description: Identify data theft or stealing information.
rubric.how: Mention that data may be stolen or copied without permission.

rubric.why: Data loss or destruction is a valid security issue.
rubric.description: Identify data loss or destruction.
rubric.how: Mention accidental or deliberate loss or destruction of data.

rubric.why: A further valid security issue earns credit, with one mark available for a clear explanation of an issue.
rubric.description: Name another valid issue, such as malware or hacking, and show understanding of its effect.
rubric.how: State another threat and briefly indicate that it can damage, expose, or disrupt data.

modelAnswer: Unauthorized access: an unauthorised person views or uses data without permission.
Data theft: information is stolen or copied without the owner's permission.
Data loss: data may be accidentally deleted or deliberately destroyed.
Viruses or other malware can damage data or interfere with access to it.

items.followUp: How can an algorithm be checked using test data?

rubric.why: Verification checks whether an algorithm is correct.
rubric.description: State that verification checks the correctness of an algorithm.
rubric.how: Use the idea of checking or ensuring correctness.

rubric.why: Tracing the steps with test data is a way to verify an algorithm.
rubric.description: Mention tracing or testing the algorithm with data and checking its result.
rubric.how: State that the algorithm is followed with test data to check its output.

modelAnswer: Algorithm verification is the process of checking that an algorithm is correct.
It can be done by tracing its steps with test data and checking that it produces the expected result.

items.followUp: What is a candidate solution to a problem?

rubric.why: A candidate solution is a proposed or possible solution to the problem.
rubric.description: Define it as a proposed or possible solution.
rubric.how: State that it is one possible answer to the problem.

rubric.why: A candidate solution must be checked to determine whether it solves the problem.
rubric.description: Explain that it is tested or evaluated for suitability.
rubric.how: Mention checking whether it meets the problem's requirements.

modelAnswer: A candidate solution is a proposed possible solution to a problem.
It is tested or evaluated to determine whether it correctly meets the problem's requirements.
